conviction_note: Zero. I found nothing the tape does not already hold. The one company-specific surprise was the Australian season: the June guide assumed normal Australian weather, and Falls Creek and Hotham then closed a month early. Stifel cut its Q4 by ~$8m and FY27 by 2% for exactly that on 2026-09-24. The pass-sales debate (units ~-10%, softer into Labor Day) sits in at least four broker notes and in an 11.5-point put skew. The 17.7%-of-float short and the activist buying are public ORTEX and EDGAR data, so they are the price rather than something missing from it.
bar: FY2026 Resort Reported EBITDA guide $735-755m (midpoint $745m), assuming 'normal weather conditions and operations throughout the Australian ski season', from the company's 8-K of 2026-06-08: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/812011/000081201126000025/a2026430pressrelease.htm. The nine-month figure is $868.0m, so the guide implies Q4 of -$113m to -$133m, against -$123.6m in Q4 FY25 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/vail-resorts-reports-fiscal-2025-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results-and-provides-fiscal-2026-outlook-302569969.html). The Q4 EPS consensus is about -$5.23 (Investing.com) or -$5.37 (Zacks), and the two sources disagree. There is no second source for the line the stock actually trades on (the pass-sales update and the FY27 guide): FY27 EBITDA consensus is unsourced; $885m was a stale pre-June figure. Any size on that line would be capped.
positioning_check: Short interest is 17.7% of free float, a series high and up 9% in one day, with 7.82 days to cover and a 0.96% borrow fee (ORTEX, data 2026-09-25: https://ortex.news/articles/173228/mtn-bears-step-up-three-days-before-the-print). It was 16.3% two days earlier (https://ortex.news/articles/172330/analysts-cut-targets-as-oasis-raises-stake-before-mtn-print). The 25-delta skew is +11.46 vol points, with puts bid. Open-interest put/call is 0.5 and the event-implied move 7.38%. Oasis added to 7.4% on 2026-09-22 in the middle of a proxy fight, and Vail hired takeover-defense bankers in June (Semafor via Colorado Sun, 2026-06-26). The short is crowded and a buyer is in the market, so any negative would have to shrink; neither fact is hidden.

outside_window.finding: Proxy fight: Oasis (7.4%) nominated four directors including Bob Chapek, for an annual meeting with no date yet (normally early December). Board control, and the possible sale of resorts that Matthew Prince is pushing, are decided after the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Australian season, dropped as a finding. It was the 5th-worst since 1954. On 2026-07-01 Spencers Creek had zero snow at the start of July, in the warmest June in 59 years (https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-07-03/snow-at-last-for-nsw-ski-season-perisher-thredbo-australia/106872456). Hotham and Falls Creek closed on 2026-09-06, a month early (https://www.weatherzone.com/au/news/historically-low-early-september-snow-depth-as-more-resorts-announce-closure/1891539). That cuts against the June guide's normal-weather assumption and management's 'encouraged by early momentum in Australia'. It is already in the estimates: Stifel cut Q4 by ~$8m and FY27 by 2% for it on 2026-09-24 (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stifel-cuts-vail-resorts-stock-price-target-on-australia-challenges-93CH-4915299). It likely lands inside the guided range (low end), and it is weather inference. The Epic Australia Pass, up 31% in dollars, is locked in and partly offsets it.

Pass sales since the June update. The -10% units estimate is on the wire: Mizuho assumes -10% steady, and UBS says sales 'softened more than previously expected into the critical Labor Day period'. BNP's web-traffic data shows no recovery. I found no independent unit data; Google Trends returned 429, and Similarweb for epicpass.com gives no year-over-year figure.

Pass pricing pages. The adult Epic Pass was $1,119 before and $1,145 after 2026-09-07. There is a 20% discount for ages 13-30 and the Epic Friend 50%-off ticket credit (August). These are known promotions and say nothing about volume.

EDGAR since 2026-06-08. The 8-Ks are a CEO podcast (7.01, 06-23), the Hornbuckle board appointment (07-30) and Decker's board exit (09-02). There are no Form 4 open-market buys after Katz's $4.9m in March 2026. None carries financial content.
Oasis 13D and DFAN14A exhibits: governance only, with no operating data and no explicit capital-return demand.
Dividend. Coverage worries appear in a GuruFocus payout-ratio note. No analyst forecasts a cut and no document signals one.
Layoffs and hiring: nothing new since the 2024-25 Resource Efficiency plan.
baseline_tension: Nothing here contradicts the baseline. The put skew, the -15.5% distance from the 52-week high and the downgrades already carry the soft pass-sales and Australia story. The record short interest and the activist buyer are the visible counterweight. The price already holds both sides, so the emitted number is 0.
lessons_applied: Dropped the Australian-season finding (draft -0.5). It is weather-to-company inference (lessons 5 and 'what has worked'), Stifel had already cut estimates for it on 2026-09-24, and it most likely lands inside the guided FY26 range (lesson 6). It is also on the reported quarter, which this name's reaction history does not pay on; the stock trades on the pass update and the guide (lesson 1). It stays only in print_vs_bar_pct at -0.5.

Dropped the crowded-short/activist-buyer positioning long (draft +0.8). Lesson 7 makes a crowded short a reason to shrink negatives, not a positive of its own. Lesson 5 says positioning and borrow are the information set, not a missed fact. Going long against an 11.5-point put skew needs a stated reason the options are wrong, and I had none beyond the positioning itself. Moved to positioning_check.

The bar for the line the stock trades on (FY27 guide and pass sales) could not be sourced to two agreeing estimates (lesson 6), so nothing could be sized there above a small cap. Net result: findings empty and expected_move 0, against a draft sum of +0.3.
